Match each blank by following the algebraic flow:

- From \(a_n=a_1+f(n)\), the next terms are naturally \(a_{n+1}=a_1+f(n+1)\) and \(a_{n+k}=a_1+f(n+k)\).
- Define \(P\) as the product of the next \(k\) terms, rewritten as \(\prod (a_n+g(j))\).
- For the coefficients of that polynomial in \(a_n\) to be nonnegative, we need \(g(j)\ge 0\).
- Then use \(a_n+g(j)=a_{n+j}=a_1+f(n+j)\), so \(g(j)=a_1+f(n+j)-a_n=a_1+f(n+j)-a_1-f(n)=f(n+j)-f(n)\), and this must be \(\ge 0\).
- Since \(f(1)=0\) because \(a_1=a_1+f(1)\), and \(g(j)\) must be independent of \(n\), \(f\) must be linear: \(f(n)=mn+b\), with intercept at \(n=0\), and then \(f(1)=m+b=0\Rightarrow b=-m\), so \(f(n)=(n-1)m\).
- Then \(m\ge 0\) integer.
- This yields \(g(j)=jm\), and hence
  \[
  \prod_{j=1}^k (a_n+jm)=P(a_n)=a_n^k+C_{k-1}a_n^{k-1}+\cdots+C_1a_n+k!m^k,
  \]
  with \(C_0=k!m^k\) and coefficients \(\ge 0\).
- Final sequence form: \(a_n=a_1+(n-1)m\), with \(a_1\ge 1\) integer and \(m\ge 0\) integer.

Answer: 1, 10, 13, 7, 22, 18, 14, 20, 11, 16, 8, 15, 9, 4, 21, 19, 3, 6, 2, 5, 17, 24, 12, 23
